text.p: Bobby Jones threw a four-hitter to become the National League's first nine-game winner as the New York Mets defeated the Montreal Expos 7-0 on Wednesday.
Jones (9-2) joined Toronto's Roger Clemens and Baltimore's Jimmy Key as the only nine-game winners in the major leagues.
He surrendered four singles, walked two and struck out seven.

"It's probably one of the better games I pitched," Jones said. "I had good command of my pitches and my fastball had some movement. We had a big inning, but they are just as capable, so regardless of the lead, you have to be careful."

Carlos Baerga sparked the offence with his first homer of the season and four RBI for the Mets, who beat Martinez (8-1) for the first time in 15 career meetings. Baerga entered the game with eight RBI in 147 at-bats.

Martinez, who had been practically unhittable this season, was tagged for seven runs -- two earned -- and seven hits in just five innings. He walked three and struck out five in his shortest outing of the season.
In Cincinnati, Kent Mercker and three relievers combined on an eight-hitter and Barry Larkin scored both runs as the Cincinnati Reds defeated the Philadelphia Phillies 2-0.
Cincinnati has won five of its last six and took three of the four games in the series from Philadelphia. Carrasco.
In his last 17-1/3 innings, Mercker (2-5), has allowed just five runs and 12 hits.
Larkin doubled in the second inning and scored on a groundout by Willie Greene. In the seventh, he singled and later scored on Joe Oliver's single.
In Pittsburgh, Steve Cooke allowed one unearned run over seven innings, and Joe Randa had a two-run double as the Pittsburgh Pirates posted a 4-1 victory over the Chicago Cubs.

Cooke (4-6) gave up five hits and one walk with six strikeouts to win for the first time since May 6th. In three outings since, the left-hander had worked 13-1/3 innings, allowing nine runs and 20 hits for a 5.41 ERA.
"The big thing is that I was able to hit my spots," said Cooke. "A lot of the time this year, I've thrown the ball up in the strike zone or right in the middle."

"Cooke just didn't make many mistakes," said Cubs manager Jim Riggleman. "He didn't give in and kept throwing the changeup. Just when you think you know what he is going to do, he'd pop the fastball. It was an extremely well-pitched game."
The Cubs scored their lone run in the seventh as Shawon Dunston reached on a fielder's choice and came home on Ryne Sandberg's double to right-centre.
